title: Electric Utilities Act, SA 2003, c E-5.1
edition: Current version: in force since 2026-02-06 (stable link canlii.ca/t/56npt)

values.where: not in source; info.json says saved 2026-10-25

values.value: SA 2025 c 26 = Bill 8 (most recent amendment listed)
values.quote: SA 2025, c 26 Utilities Statutes Amendment Act, 2025 (Bill 8, assented to 2025-12-11)

(vv.1) “self-supply” means the production of electric energy on a property of which a person is the owner or a tenant where any of the electric energy is consumed on that property by that owner or tenant

the portion of electric energy that is self-supply produced on a property of which a person is the owner or a tenant and that is consumed solely on that property by that owner or tenant, except in respect of a rate ...

All electric energy entering or leaving the interconnected electric system must be exchanged through the power pool unless section 39(1.1) or 105(1.1) apply or regulations made under section 41, section 99 or section 142 provide otherwise.

unsupported_wording: s. 2(1)(b) is a partial exemption: the source adds 'except in respect of a rate included in a tariff approved by the Commission ... section 122(2)(b)', which the claim omits. Regulations are under ss. 41, 99 and 142 (claim does not list them). 'Surplus ... goes through the power pool or the micro-generation rules; there is no separate export right' is an inference, not stated; the Micro-generation Regulation (Alta Reg 27/2008) is only listed in the regulations panel.
note: File is the cited CanLII consolidation. Regulations panel also lists a Data Centre Regulation, Alta Reg 117/2026, not mentioned in the claim. Read date is not in the source.

publisher: New York City Landmarks Preservation Commission
title: Permit - Certificate of Appropriateness COFA-19-24537, 50 Hudson Street, Manhattan (Tribeca West Historic District)
unsupported_wording: The phrase 'installing mechanical units set behind a louvered screen' is verbatim (p. 1). But the not-visible finding refers to 'the mechanical bulkhead and glass-clad penthouse will not be visibile from any public throughfare', not explicitly to the screened mechanical units; the overall rooftop addition is described as 'visible'. 'Not documented as a data centre' is correct: the permit describes an office/warehouse building and does not mention a data centre.
note: Main approved work is a two-storey glass-brick rooftop addition.
